To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we introduce general abstractions and efficient algorithms for solving mixed domain and mixed-dimensional finite element problems.

we introduce a novel mathematical software framework for the solution of mixed domain and/or mixed dimensional partial differential equations, which we have implemented and tested in the FEniCs software.

(i) we have developed a general framework for the efficient solution of mixed dimensional and mixed domain PDEs; (ii) this framework is applicable for PDEs of arbitrary codimension; and (iii) we have implemented this framework in a widely used finite element software.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing general mathematical abstractions and efficient algorithms for mixed domain finite element methods.

developing a general and efficient mathematical framework for mixed domain finite elements, which we hope will facilitate the development and use of mixed domain PDEs for scientific and engineering problems.
abstractions and algorithms to enable automated solution of a broad class of mixed domain and/or mixed dimensional partial differential equations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the new abstractions and algorithms presented in this article enable a more flexible and powerful approach to the discretization, solution, and postprocessing of a wide range of mixed domain and coupled PDEs, and that they can be readily implemented in existing finite element software.
we present a new and general framework for the discretization and solution of mixed domain and/or mixed dimensional PDE systems.
the presented abstractions and algorithms are a step towards a unified framework for mixed domain and mixed dimension finite element methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed new mathematical abstractions and efficient numerical algorithms for solving coupled systems of partial differential equations with mixed dimensional domains.
we present abstractions and algorithms that enable efficient and flexible finite element methods for mixed dimensional problems.
we provide a general mathematical abstraction for mixed dimensional problems and a corresponding set of efficient algorithms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FEniCs framework is capable of supporting the development of efficient, flexible, and general-purpose finite element solvers for mixed domain and mixed-dimensional PDEs.
a unified approach to the discretization and solution of mixed dimensional problems is possible and practical, and can be implemented in a way that is accessible to a broad community of users.
a general framework can be developed to handle mixed domain PDE discretizations.
